claims: On March 20/21, 2026, Muslims are celebrating Eid al-Fitr.
Eid al-Fitr is the "Feast of Fast-Breaking".
Eid al-Fitr marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr is a three-day celebration.
Eid al-Fitr involves early morning prayers.
Eid al-Fitr involves wearing new clothes.
Eid al-Fitr involves sharing feasts with family and friends.
Eid al-Fitr celebrates the completion of a month of fasting, spiritual reflection, and increased devotion.
Eid Prayers are special communal prayers held early in the morning.
Zakat al-Fitr (or Fitrana) is given to the poor to ensure they can participate in the celebration.
Eid al-Fitr festivities include visiting family and friends.
Eid al-Fitr festivities include giving gifts (often money to children).
Eid al-Fitr festivities include wearing new clothes.
Eid al-Fitr is known as the "Sweet Festival" for the special desserts and treats made to celebrate.
Greetings for Eid al-Fitr are "Eid Mubarak" (Blessed Eid) or "Eid Sa'id" (Happy Eid).
The exact date of Eid al-Fitr can vary slightly based on local sightings of the crescent moon.
